title: Tomas carries the stone from the church
summary: Tomas of Måsabacka carried the stone from near Nedervetil church to the road junction, and it took his name.
note: Distance: OCR '3 4 km' in Budkavlen, 3/4 km in Stejskal.

title: Nuija-Heikki carries the stone up the rock
summary: Nuija-Heikki carried the huge stone from the bog up onto the rock; the yearbook notes it is far too big for that.

title: Poras-äijä throws the väkikivi over the fence
summary: Finding men straining at a great väkikivi, Poras-äijä threw it over the fence: 'A man ought not to bother lifting a thing like that!'

title: Siltalan Kustavi throws the village stone
summary: Only two village men could move the väkikivi; young Kustavi of Siltala threw it over the fence, and the men took it badly.

title: Antti Nousiainen tosses the stone over the manor fence
summary: Antti Nousiainen secretly tossed the former väkikivi over the tall fence of the manor avenue.

title: Iso Rönkkö's stone on Nostokiven kallio
summary: Iso Rönkkö carried a stone under his arm from Lehtoniemi field and dropped it by the road: 'The man who lifts that is neither poor nor weak.' The rock was named after it; Taavetti of Rönkkölä lifted it, but not with a folding knife on top. Jussi of Lähdeniemi had it dragged into a mud pit.

title: The pregnant hostess of Perho
summary: A Perho hostess lifted the village's largest väkikivi while pregnant; her daughter later lifted it with a second stone on top.

title: Lemetti's strength lives in his väkikivi
summary: Lemetti Järvenpää of Haapajärvi, dead two hundred years, still lives on in his väkikivi, now the porch step of the old Istula farm.
note: Stone 'Lemmetin väkikivi' has no record yet.

title: Tohni rolls a stone onto the church wall
summary: Tohni took part in building Kyrö church and rolled onto its wall, alone, a stone ten men could not move.

title: Peltoniemen Paavo
summary: A fictional character's youthful hobby of lifting väkikivi.
note: Same story printed three times; not evidence of any stone.
